description: On 2016-2020 Acura MDX with the 3.5L V6 (J35Y5) and Auto Idle-Stop, the engine may fail to automatically restart from a stop event, leaving the driver stranded in traffic. NHTSA opened an Engineering Analysis (PE22-016 → EA) after 1,300+ complaints across ~2.2M Honda/Acura vehicles, with 4 confirmed accidents. Acura issued Service Bulletin 23-001 in January 2023 with a PGM-FI software update (reduces idle-stop operating range) and extended warranty coverage on starter replacement and valve adjustment to 10 years / unlimited miles. Note: the Sport Hybrid (J30Y1) uses a different motor-based stop/start system and is not in scope of this TSB.
solution: Have dealer perform the PGM-FI idle-stop software update plus starter / starter relay inspection per Honda's 2023 service campaign (covered 10 years). To avoid recurrence, defeat Idle-Stop with the dash button each drive or install an aftermarket auto-disable module.

description: Certain 2018-2020 MDX (J35Y5 3.5L V6) and MDX Sport Hybrid (3.0L V6 hybrid) units were built with low-density, improperly molded in-tank fuel pump impellers. Surface cracking from production solvent absorption causes the impeller to swell and seize against the pump body, leading to no-start or stall while driving. Honda issued NHTSA recall 23V-858 covering ~2.5 million Honda/Acura vehicles.
solution: Free recall remedy under NHTSA 23V-858 - dealer replaces the fuel pump module with a redesigned part. Check VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or owners.acura.com and schedule replacement immediately if not yet completed.

description: The AcuraLink infotainment system in third-gen MDX models experiences random reboots during driving, temporarily disabling navigation, audio, and the backup camera. The system takes 30-60 seconds to restart, leaving the driver without audio or navigation guidance mid-route.
solution: Update to the latest infotainment firmware from an Acura dealer. Reset the system to factory defaults and clear cached data. If reboots continue, the infotainment control module may need hardware replacement under an extended warranty program.

description: Third-generation MDX models with the ZF 9-speed automatic suffer from torque converter shudder during light throttle acceleration between 30-50 mph. The lockup clutch in the torque converter vibrates as it engages, creating a sensation similar to driving over rumble strips that many owners mistake for an engine misfire.
solution: Update the TCM software to the latest Acura calibration that modifies torque converter lockup strategy. Perform a complete ATF drain and refill with Honda DW-1. If shudder persists after software update and fluid change, the torque converter assembly must be replaced.

description: The ZF 9HP 9-speed automatic introduced on the 2016 MDX suffers from documented hesitation, harsh shifts, lurching, and unexpected downshifts/deceleration. Drivers report the vehicle hesitating from a stop, banging into gear, or briefly losing power. Software miscommunication between TCM, ECM and throttle control is the alleged root cause; a class action was filed alleging Honda knew of the defect from 2015.
solution: Have dealer apply latest TCM/PGM-FI software updates first (covered by powertrain warranty). If symptoms persist, request fluid replacement and dealer escalation; document everything for lemon-law/class-action relief. Avoid jerky throttle inputs while cold.

description: 2019-2020 Nautilus models with the base 2.0L EcoBoost (non-hybrid) suffer unexplained coolant loss, white tailpipe smoke, an overheat warning, and sometimes coolant intrusion into the cylinders. Ford TSB 20-2234 traces the most common cause to a failing exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) cooler that leaks coolant internally; the related design also has a known coolant-intrusion weakness (narrow coolant slit between cylinders compromising the head-gasket seal). Owners report repeated coolant top-offs with no visible external leak, then misfires as coolant fouls the plugs. A June 2025 Ford EcoBoost coolant-intrusion class action covers 1.5L-2.0L engines; the most severe Nautilus cases require engine replacement with the redesigned block.
solution: Per TSB 20-2234, perform a cooling-system pressure test and inspect the EGR cooler; replace the EGR cooler and update PCM software for the typical case. If a coolant smell, white smoke, and cylinder misfires persist (coolant intrusion past the head gasket), the durable fix is a long-block / engine replacement with the updated cross-drilled block — a head-gasket-only repair on the old-style block will fail again. Replace fouled spark plugs and flush the cooling system.

description: Nautilus models built on or before March 11, 2021 with the 8F35 8-speed automatic commonly exhibit a shudder, buck, hesitation, or jerk while accelerating from a stop up to about 35 mph (57 km/h). Ford Technical Service Bulletin 21-2389 (superseding 21-2081) attributes the condition primarily to PCM/transmission solenoid control software rather than internal mechanical wear, though severe untreated cases progressed to harsh shifting and, in a minority of CarComplaints reports, complete transmission failure. This is the single most-complained-about Nautilus problem and is the subject of a Chimicles Schwartz Kriner class-action investigation covering 2019-2021 Edge/Nautilus 8F35 vehicles.
solution: First-line fix per TSB 21-2389 is to reprogram the PCM with the latest software level and update the transmission solenoid (adaptive) strategy (about 0.9 hours labor, typically covered under the 6yr/70k powertrain warranty). If the shudder persists after reprogramming, the shop should inspect for a failing torque converter, worn clutch packs, or contaminated fluid and replace as needed. A transmission fluid service with the correct Mercon ULV is recommended at the same time.

description: Nautilus owners frequently report the Auto Start-Stop system behaving erratically — failing to engage, failing to auto-restart smoothly at the light, or throwing a system-fault/malfunction message. The most common root cause is the 12V battery state-of-charge falling below the threshold the system needs (the AGM start-stop battery degrades faster than a conventional battery), so the system disables itself or restarts roughly. The popularity of plug-and-play 'start-stop eliminator' modules for the Nautilus reflects how much the behavior annoys owners.
solution: Test the 12V battery and charging system; replace a weak or aged AGM battery with the correct spec and perform a Battery Monitoring System (BMS) reset so the PCM relearns state-of-charge. Ensure parasitic-draw and software are current. Owners who simply dislike the feature use the dash defeat button each drive or a plug-and-play disable module (not a repair, a preference).

description: 2019 and 2020 Lincoln Nautilus crossovers are covered by NHTSA recall 25V442000, Ford's campaign 25S72, for a rearview camera software defect. The fault has two possible presentations: the camera can show a blank image instead of the view behind the vehicle, or the rearview image can remain on the center display even after the driver has finished backing and shifted out of reverse. Ford describes the safety consequence directly — a blank image reduces the driver's view behind the Nautilus, and a stale image left on screen can distract the driver — and says either can increase the risk of a crash. Note that this is a separate action from the earlier Nautilus backup-camera recall; if your VIN shows 25V442000 open, that campaign has its own remedy regardless of any camera work done previously.
solution: Take the Nautilus to a Lincoln dealer for a free rearview camera software update. There is no cost to the owner and no part to buy. Owner notification letters went out September 4, 2025. To confirm whether your specific vehicle still needs the update — especially if the SUV was bought used or has had prior camera-related recall work — run the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and look for campaign 25V442000. Ford's customer line is 1-866-436-7332 and the internal reference is 25S72.

description: First-generation Nautilus owners widely report the SYNC 3 center touchscreen freezing, going completely black, or spontaneously rebooting while driving — sometimes leaving only the backup camera working. Symptoms point to memory corruption in the APIM (Accessory Protocol Interface Module / SYNC module) software rather than the display panel itself, so a black or frozen screen usually traces to the APIM. Distinct from the 2024+ panoramic/center-display reboot recall (25V337), which is the newer multimedia module on the redesigned model.
solution: Try a SYNC master reset (hold the power/volume button and Seek-Right for 10 seconds) and install the latest SYNC 3 software via USB or OTA. If freezes recur, the APIM module is reprogrammed or replaced by the dealer; updating to the current software level resolves most memory-related lockups. A pending USB drive update can also stop the reboot loop.

description: NHTSA recall 26V331 and Nissan campaign PMA66 apply to 51,598 model-year 2025-2026 Kicks vehicles produced June 24, 2024 through January 9, 2026. A combination-meter software logic error can cause communication loss between the graphic controller and automotive controller during cold start, producing a partial, blue or blank display and hiding required telltales and indicators. Nissan reported seven technical reports and 205 warranty claims, not owner-report totals.
solution: Check the VIN for 26V331/PMA66. Nissan dealers update the combination-meter software with CONSULT 4 at no charge; the Part 573 report estimates about 0.5 hour and lists July 1, 2026 as the planned owner-notification date. Do not buy a cluster, display, controller, wiring harness or software product from this page; recall eligibility and the official software remedy must be confirmed first.

description: NHTSA recall 25V324 covers certain 2025 Kicks and Frontier vehicles with an affected Center Information Display. A software logic error can cause a communication error with the In-Vehicle Infotainment module, leaving the rearview monitor blank in reverse and reducing rearward visibility. The combined population is 79,755 vehicles; the exact Kicks production window is June 24, 2024 through March 7, 2025, and eligibility remains VIN-specific.
solution: Check the VIN for 25V324/PMA48. Nissan dealers update the Center Information Display software through CONSULT 3+ and a Nissan-provided jumper harness at no charge; the Part 573 report lists July 1, 2025 as the planned owner-notification date. Do not buy a camera, Center Information Display, IVI module, harness or software product from this page; recall eligibility and the official software remedy must be confirmed first.

description: Kicks owners report the infotainment touchscreen freezing or becoming unresponsive (requiring a restart), the system randomly rebooting on its own, and frequent Apple CarPlay / Android Auto disconnections, failures to connect, or audio that cuts out after a few minutes. The failures are predominantly software-related rather than hardware faults, and a dealer software update (TSB NTB23-018) addresses many cases.
solution: Try a certified USB data cable, inspect the USB port for debris, and restart both the phone and the head unit (hold the power/volume knob ~10-20 seconds); ensure phone OS and vehicle infotainment firmware are current. If freezing or random reboots persist, have a Nissan dealer apply the latest infotainment/audio firmware update (per TSB) or diagnose the head unit.

description: Third-generation Muranos with Nissan's Forward Emergency Braking (FEB)/Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) have widely reported 'phantom braking' — the system suddenly and forcefully brakes when no obstacle is present, creating rear-end collision and loss-of-control risk. The problem is associated with the front grille radar/sensor module (Bosch-supplied) misreading the road. The Murano is named in AEB class-action litigation alongside other Nissan models, and Nissan issued TSBs addressing false AEB/FCW activation on 2019-2024 Murano (Z52).
solution: Dealer diagnosis per the applicable TSB; remedies have included radar sensor recalibration, software/ECU reprogramming, or sensor replacement. Keep the front emblem/grille radar area clean and free of obstructions (snow, mud, badges). The FEB system can be temporarily disabled via the vehicle settings menu while driving in conditions that trigger false activation.

description: A recurring owner complaint on newer Nissan crossovers, including Murano, is a dead battery after sitting overnight or for a few days despite the battery testing good initially. Reports often point to parasitic draw from telematics, AV control, or body control modules that fail to enter sleep mode, sometimes accompanied by app connectivity glitches or infotainment oddities. The issue can be intermittent, making it difficult to catch unless a proper draw test is performed after module timeout.
solution: Start with battery state-of-health and charging-system checks, then perform a parasitic draw test with the vehicle fully asleep. If draw remains excessive, isolate the circuit by pulling fuses and checking telematics, AV, and BCM-related branches; software updates, module resets, or replacement of the offending module may be required. Replacing the battery alone often provides only temporary relief if the root draw remains.

description: Owners have reported the driver's seat rocking front-to-back, clicking during braking/acceleration, or feeling loose on its track. Nissan has issued service information on seat track/frame-related movement complaints on late-model vehicles, and owner reports indicate the issue can appear at relatively low mileage. The problem is usually caused by play in the seat track assembly, frame hardware, or worn internal seat adjuster components rather than the floor mounting points themselves.
solution: Road-test the vehicle and confirm whether the movement occurs during throttle tip-in, braking, or over bumps. Inspect seat track bolts, rail alignment, and the seat adjuster assembly; repairs typically involve tightening hardware to spec, replacing the seat track/adjuster assembly, or replacing the seat frame if internal play is present. If the seat has power functions, verify all positions after repair and recalibrate memory settings if equipped.

description: Nissan NTB19-033G applies to 2015-2024 Murano Z52 vehicles when ICC stops working, the AEB/FEB warning illuminates, or a front-radar obstruction message appears and C1A16, C1A16-97, C2582 or C2582-97 is the only stored DTC. Its flow separates obstruction and weather from repeat incidents, sensor manufacture date, replacement where authorized and required sensor alignment. The frozen 2021-2024 page is inside that exact boundary.
solution: Preserve all DTCs and confirm whether obstruction or severe weather explains the event. Use NTB19-033G only when one listed radar DTC is the sole stored code; the bulletin repeatedly says not to replace the distance sensor outside its flow. When replacement is authorized, use the EPC for the VIN-specific sensor and perform alignment. Do not buy a radar sensor or bracket from this page; DTC state, manufacture date, diagnosis, calibration and VIN fitment must be established first.

description: Multiple Murano owners in the 2021-2024 range have reported the backup camera showing a black screen, frozen image, blue screen, or distorted picture when shifting into reverse. This is also covered by Nissan/NHTSA recall actions affecting rearview camera display reliability on Nissan vehicles, including Murano, because the image may not display as required by FMVSS 111. Owners typically experience intermittent failure at first, then more frequent loss of image, especially after startup or in hot/cold weather.
solution: Confirm the concern by repeatedly cycling ignition and selecting reverse while monitoring the display. Diagnosis usually involves checking for AV control unit software/hardware faults, camera harness connection issues, and camera module failure; Nissan recall/TSB procedures generally call for software update, AV control unit reprogramming, or replacement of the camera/control unit if the image remains unstable. If the vehicle is covered by an open recall, the recall remedy should be completed before paid repairs.
